Maya: FYI PR #5301 updates Go/TS/Py snippets to show cursor resume + retry helper. Docs CI failing on snippet lint.
Ravi: link?
Maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5301
Lin: root cause: Go example didn't persist next_cursor and used time.Sleep in example. linter blocks sync sleeps in async contexts.
Maya: proposed tiny Go iterator:
```go
ctx := context.Background()
iter := client.Stream(ctx, StreamParams{Prompt: "hello"})
for iter.Next() {
  part := iter.Value()
  fmt.Print(part.Text)
}
// save iter.ResumeToken() to resume later
// wrap call with client.Retry(ctx, func() error { ... }) for transient errors
```
Maya: Python version (async generator + retry helper):
```python
async def stream(prompt):
    async for chunk in client.responses.stream({"prompt": prompt}):
        print(chunk.text, end="")
# use client.utils.retry_async to re-run on network errors and preserve resume_token
```
Ravi: TS snippet:
```ts
for await (const msg of client.responses.stream({prompt})) {
  process.stdout.write(msg.text)
}
// store msg.resume_token from final object
```
Lin: note: include a one-line migration blurb in the examples folder about v1->v2 cursor behavior (token rename). keep it short.
Maya: I'll update PR to swap examples, add changelog entry, and a small smoke test that loads snippets and checks compile (no network).
